business_problem: Meltwater needed a faster way to understand user behavior and guide product decisions as it broke down a monolithic media-listening platform into cloud-based microservices.
solution_summary: Meltwater used MongoDB Atlas and MongoDB Charts to make product development more data-driven while the company transitioned from a monolith to a cloud-first microservices architecture on AWS. The Cosmos team built a tracking service on Atlas to capture how users interact with the application, especially around homepage onboarding and global search. MongoDB Charts sits directly on that Atlas data so product owners and engineers can run complex aggregations, visualize usage patterns, and answer detailed UX questions without exporting data to RedShift or waiting on BI teams. That tight integration is central to Meltwater’s operating model: developers can provision services quickly in Atlas, use the same operational store for analytics, and iterate on dashboards in minutes as product questions arise. By putting behavioral telemetry and visualization in one workflow, Meltwater turned product instrumentation into an everyday engineering tool rather than a separate reporting project.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Meltwater’s product-usage tracking data and supports the cloud-first microservices environment.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Charts
solution_components.role: Visualizes user-journey and feature-usage data so product and engineering teams can make decisions from live metrics.

data_flow: User interaction events are captured into MongoDB Atlas by Meltwater’s tracking service, queried with aggregations, and surfaced through MongoDB Charts dashboards that product owners and engineers use to drive roadmap and UX decisions.
business_outcome: Meltwater moved from releasing features every six months to multiple times per day, created dashboards in less than a day, and gave product teams immediate access to the metrics they need for faster UX and roadmap decisions.
metrics: Meltwater serves 30,000 customers in over 120 countries and has over 2,000 employees.
Meltwater went from releases every six months to multiple releases per day.
Once the tracking service was connected to Atlas, it took less than a day to create the two primary dashboards.
